exposure: Perinatal Institute's Growth Assessment Protocol (GAP) program
Exposure to the GAP program (before vs. after implementation)
The Perinatal Institute's Growth Assessment Protocol (GAP) program
outcome: Small for gestational age (SGA) detection rate
Admission to Neonatal Intensive and Special Care nursery (NISC)
cohort: 1818 women who delivered at The Royal Women's Hospital, Melbourne (882 after and 936 before the implementation of the GAP program)
finding: The introduction of the Perinatal Institute's Growth Assessment Protocol (GAP) program was associated with a significant increase in the detection of small for gestational age (SGA) infants without an increase in false-positive rates.
mod_finding: Following the introduction of the GAP Program, SGA babies were more likely to be born by vaginal delivery. There was no overall increase in the induction of labour or caesarean delivery rates.
